objects.original: Objective f, supplied gradient trajectory, minimizer, positive PL modulus.
objects.reconstructed: f, X, z, alpha, and a finite horizon T.
objects.evidence: The gradient is the Riesz representative of the actual derivative of f. The proof composes that derivative with the dynamics; no scalar dissipation premise replaces the trajectory.

domains.reconstructed: Complete real inner-product space E; X is represented on R, with hypotheses and results restricted to the specified forward interval.
domains.evidence: Finite-dimensional Euclidean space satisfies the typeclasses. The Hilbert-space generalization is explicitly disclosed in candidate_assumptions and lesson. A total-function encoding does not require negative-time dynamics.

quantifiers.original: Every supplied flow and every nonnegative observation time; PL at every spatial point.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For arbitrary E,f,X,z,alpha,T satisfying the hypotheses, dissipation at all t in [0,T), and decay at all t in [0,T]; PL at every x:E.
quantifiers.evidence: For a supplied global classical flow, choose any finite T at least the requested decay time, and strictly greater for dissipation. No existential trajectory quantifier is introduced or discharged.

assumptions.original: Section 2 uses C2 regularity and an attained minimum; Definition 2.5 uses C1 and positive alpha.
assumptions.reconstructed: Everywhere Frechet differentiability, global minimizer z, alpha>0, T>=0, closed-interval continuity of X, right gradient derivative on [0,T), and the global numerical PL inequality.
assumptions.evidence: On the source Euclidean domain, C2 implies the required differentiability. Classical supplied dynamics imply right dynamics and interval continuity. The relaxation is accurately declared; no smoothness or scalar energy identity is hidden in the conclusion. Completeness supplies Riesz representation and holds automatically in the source domain.

conclusion.original: Objective derivative is minus gradient norm squared, and objective gap has exponential decay with rate 2 alpha.
conclusion.reconstructed: Right objective derivative before T and the same exponential upper bound through T, together with nonnegative gap.
conclusion.evidence: The exponent and initial gap agree algebraically. Nonnegativity follows directly from global minimality. At classical source trajectories the right derivative identifies the ordinary derivative; the generalized lesson correctly labels it right-sided.

scopes.original: Conditional supplied-flow convergence; well-posedness is left aside.
scopes.reconstructed: Derivative statement on [0,T), value statement on [0,T], PL on all E; no existence, uniqueness, negative-time dynamics, or terminal derivative assertion.
scopes.evidence: The module, blind reconstruction and lesson all use these exact scopes. The reference to Ici t is a local right-derivative filter; for t<T it does not impose remote post-T dynamics. T=0 leaves dissipation empty and gives the exact initial value bound. Arbitrary finite horizons recover each source observation time under a supplied global flow.

constant_dependencies.original: PL normalization is 2 alpha; decay prefactor is the initial objective gap.
constant_dependencies.evidence: No dimension, smoothness constant, time-horizon prefactor, or auxiliary comparison constant enters the bound. Gronwall is used with K=-(2*alpha) and zero forcing.

review_evidence: Independent examination was limited to the anti-anchored reviewer packet and primary source https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07006v1#S2, Section 2 conventions, Lemma 2.1, Definition 2.5, and Corollary 2.6. The packet code derives the energy identity by chain rule, constructs continuous gap data, applies the right-slope Gronwall theorem with coefficient -2 alpha and zero forcing, and obtains gap nonnegativity from IsMinOn. The lesson follows these proof steps and states its exact wider assumptions. This is a scoped source-support decision after the declared generalization and finite-horizon elaboration, not a claim that the generalized Lean statement is textually identical to the Euclidean source. Compiler execution and test evidence are outside this independent source review. Verdict classification clarification: the generalized Hilbert-space theorem is not equivalent to the source theorem as a universally quantified proposition. The allowed domain-mismatch verdict records this genuine, explicitly documented extension; its domain and assumption slot relations remain unchanged. Source-support acceptance concerns the stated conditional Euclidean supplied-flow obligation as a specialization, not equality of the full generalized theorem with the source.

source_review.evidence: The source binding supports the conditional supplied-flow dissipation and PL rate obligation. The current module, lesson, formula proof and explicit assumption differences agree. All seven semantic slots were audited; no undeclared mathematical assumption or required source repair was found. No repair overlay is accepted by this review. The domain-mismatch verdict denotes the disclosed Hilbert-space generalization.
